---

## Background

The HCP temperature standard for RM 6 on Whychus Creek is a 7-day average daily
maximum (7DADM) of 20°C. Camp Polk is the upstream flow gage, managed by OWRD, and used in the model to forecast instream temperature at at RM 8.5 — but only within limits set by air temperature
and solar load. This document uses the Random Forest models from the operational daily
forecast to answer three questions:

> **Q1: How much Camp Polk flow is needed to keep RM 8.5 7DADM at or below 20°C?**

> **Q2: How early does that flow action need to start — and does waiting cost compliance?**

> **Q3: When in the summer season is flow management actually effective, and when does
> atmospheric heating dominate regardless of what Camp Polk releases?**

---

## Settings

```{r settings}
target_C       <- 20.0
analysis_start <- as.Date("2024-06-01")
analysis_end   <- as.Date("2024-09-30")
lead_days_vec  <- c(1, 3, 7)
model_dir      <- here("output")
```

---

## 1. Historical RM 8.5 Exceedances

```{r rm85-daily}
# Full-history daily max and 7DADM at RM 8.5
# TODO: use whychusModel::rm_8_5_historical
rm85_dadm_all <- whychusModel::rm_8_5_historical |> 
  filter(statistic %in% c("max", "7DADM")) |> 
  pivot_wider(id_cols = date, names_from = "statistic", values_from = "temperature") |> 
  rename(tmax = max,
         dadm_7 = `7DADM`)

# 2024 analysis window
rm85_daily_max <- rm85_dadm_all |>
  filter(date >= analysis_start, date <= analysis_end)

# Anchor event: peak 7DADM exceedance in 2024
anchor_row  <- rm85_daily_max |> filter(dadm_7 > target_C) |> slice_max(dadm_7, n = 1)
anchor_date <- anchor_row$date
anchor_dadm <- round(anchor_row$dadm_7, 1)
anchor_year <- year(anchor_date)
```

From 2012 through 2025, RM 8.5 has exceeded the 20°C HCP threshold on
**`r nrow(filter(rm85_dadm_all, dadm_7 > target_C, !is.na(dadm_7)))`** days.
Exceedances are concentrated in the mid-June through August window and vary
considerably by year, with some summers largely compliant and others sustaining
multi-week exceedance periods.

```{r exceedance-timeseries, fig.cap="**Figure 1.** Full-record RM 8.5 7-day average daily maximum temperature (7DADM). Orange line = 7DADM; red shading = periods exceeding the 20°C HCP threshold (dashed line). Exceedances cluster in mid-summer and vary considerably year to year."}
exceed_ts <- rm85_dadm_all |>
  filter(!is.na(dadm_7))

ggplot(exceed_ts, aes(x = date, y = dadm_7)) +
  geom_line(color = "#e67e22", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = target_C, linetype = "dashed",
             color = "#c0392b", linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text",
           x    = min(exceed_ts$date, na.rm = TRUE) + 60,
           y    = target_C + 0.3,
           label = "20°C HCP threshold",
           hjust = 0, color = "#c0392b", size = 3.2) +
  labs(title    = "RM 8.5 7DADM — full record (2012–2025)",
       x = NULL, y = "7DADM temperature (°C)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

## 2. A 2024 Exceedance — Setting the Stage

```{r cp-temp-model}
# TODO: this could potentially be better -- current r2 is 0.2
# Camp Polk flow → temperature relationship (warm season, Jun–Sep).
# Used as a delta: given a flow change from q_obs to q, the model estimates how much
# Camp Polk 7DADM changes. The observed temperature is preserved as the baseline so that
# the thermal state of the system on each run date is respected.

# Agree that this is an area of improvement, some thoughts include - where would the flow action be occurring, assumping TSID diversion. We could model the change in temperature resulting from flow left instream in the reach between TSID and Camp Polk rather than the direct relationship between flow and temperature at CP. 

cp_flow_temp_hist <- camp_polk_flow_historical |>
  filter(statistic == "mean") |> select(date, flow_cfs) |>
  inner_join(
    camp_polk_temperature_historical |>
      filter(statistic == "7DADM") |>
      mutate(date = as.Date(date)) |>
      select(date, cp_7dadm = temperature),
    by = "date"
  ) |>
  filter(month(date) %in% 6:9, !is.na(flow_cfs), !is.na(cp_7dadm))

cp_temp_lm <- lm(cp_7dadm ~ log(flow_cfs), data = cp_flow_temp_hist)
summary(cp_temp_lm)

# Returns the model-predicted temperature at flow q (used only to compute deltas)
cp_temp_at_flow <- function(q) {
  as.numeric(predict(cp_temp_lm, newdata = data.frame(flow_cfs = pmax(q, 1))))
}

# Adjust observed temperature by the model-predicted change from baseline flow q_obs to q
cp_temp_delta <- function(t_obs, q, q_obs) {
  t_obs + (cp_temp_at_flow(q) - cp_temp_at_flow(q_obs))
}
```

The peak 7DADM in summer 2024 occurred on **`r format(anchor_date, "%B %d, %Y")`**, reaching
**`r anchor_dadm`°C** — `r round(anchor_dadm - target_C, 1)`°C above the 20°C standard.
This event anchors the worked example in the next section.

```{r anchor-plot, fig.cap="**Figure 4.** RM 8.5 temperature and Camp Polk flow over summer 2024. Orange line = 7DADM; grey line = daily max; blue bars = mean daily Camp Polk flow (right axis). The red shaded band highlights the 7-day averaging window that produced the peak exceedance. The dashed red line marks the 20°C HCP threshold."}
band_start     <- anchor_date - 6
cp_flow_window <- camp_polk_flow_historical |>
  filter(statistic == "mean", date >= analysis_start, date <= analysis_end)
flow_scale <- max(cp_flow_window$flow_cfs, na.rm = TRUE) /
              max(rm85_daily_max$tmax, na.rm = TRUE)

rm85_daily_max |>
  ggplot(aes(x = date)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = band_start, xmax = anchor_date,
           ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "#c0392b", alpha = 0.08) +
  geom_col(data = cp_flow_window,
           aes(x = date, y = flow_cfs / flow_scale),
           fill = "#2c7bb6", alpha = 0.35, width = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = tmax),   color = "#7f8c8d", linewidth = 0.6, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_line(aes(y = dadm_7), color = "#e67e22", linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = target_C, linetype = "dashed",
             color = "#c0392b", linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("point", x = anchor_date, y = anchor_dadm,
           shape = 21, size = 4, fill = "#c0392b", color = "white", stroke = 1.5) +
  annotate("text", x = anchor_date + 1, y = anchor_dadm + 0.3,
           label = sprintf("%s\n7DADM = %.1f°C", format(anchor_date, "%b %d"), anchor_dadm),
           hjust = 0, color = "#c0392b", size = 3.2) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name     = "Temperature (°C)",
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . * flow_scale, name = "Camp Polk flow (cfs)",
                        labels = scales::comma)
  ) +
  labs(title    = "RM 8.5 temperature & Camp Polk flow — summer 2024",
       subtitle = "Grey = daily max  |  Orange = 7DADM  |  Blue bars = Camp Polk mean daily flow",
       x = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y.right = element_text(color = "#2c7bb6"),
        axis.text.y.right  = element_text(color = "#2c7bb6"))
```

## 3. What Flow Would Have Prevented the Exceedance?

For each forecast lead (1, 3, and 7 days before the anchor event), air temperature and
cloud cover are fixed at their observed historical values. Camp Polk flow is swept across
the 5th–95th percentile of the observed record (`cp_flow_mean` and `cp_flow_m1` swept
together — a sustained 2-day flow scenario), and Camp Polk water temperature (`cp_7dadm`,
`cp_7dadm_m1`) is co-varied with flow using a log-linear regression fit to warm-season
historical data (`r sprintf("cp\\_7dadm = %.2f + %.2f × log(flow)", coef(cp_temp_lm)[1], coef(cp_temp_lm)[2])`,
R² = `r round(summary(cp_temp_lm)$r.squared, 2)`). The crossing point at 20°C is the
minimum sustained flow estimated to prevent exceedance at that lead.

```{r anchor-sweep-prep}
get_wx <- function(d, var, k) {
  v <- all_historical_forecasts |>
    filter(valid_date == d, variable == var) |>
    filter(lead_days == k) |> 
    pull(value)
    # summarise(out = fn(value, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
    #pull(out)
  if (length(v) == 0 || is.nan(v)) NA_real_ else v
}
#first_val <- function(x) if (length(x) > 0) x[[1]] else NA_real_

base_feats <- map(lead_days_vec, function(k) {
  run_date <- anchor_date - k
  list(
    k           = k,
    run_date    = run_date,
    obs_flow    = camp_polk_flow_historical |>
                    filter(statistic == "mean", date == run_date) |> pull(flow_cfs),
    cp_7dadm    = camp_polk_temperature_historical |>
                    filter(statistic == "7DADM", date == run_date) |> pull(temperature),
    Julian      = yday(run_date),
    air_max     = get_wx(run_date,     "temperature_2m_max", k),
    air_min     = get_wx(run_date,     "temperature_2m_min", k),
    cloud_pct   = get_wx(run_date,     "cloud_cover_mean", k),
    cp_7dadm_m1 = camp_polk_temperature_historical |>
                    filter(statistic == "7DADM", date == run_date - 1) |> pull(temperature),
    air_max_m1  = get_wx(run_date - 1, "temperature_2m_max", k),
    air_min_m1  = get_wx(run_date - 1, "temperature_2m_min", k),
    dadm_m1     = rm85_dadm_all |> filter(date == run_date - 1) |> pull(dadm_7)
  )
})
```

```{r anchor-sweep-run}
flow_range <- quantile(camp_polk_flow_historical$flow_cfs, c(0.05, 0.95), na.rm = TRUE)
flow_grid  <- seq(flow_range[1], flow_range[2], length.out = 300)

sweep_df <- map_dfr(base_feats, function(bf) {
  rf <- readRDS(file.path(model_dir, sprintf("rm85_rf_7dadm_lead%d.rds", bf$k)))
  map_dfr(flow_grid, function(q) {
    
    # Pre-compute adjusted CP temps so they can be used in both feat and the output tibble
    calc_cp_7dadm    <- cp_temp_delta(bf$cp_7dadm,    q, bf$obs_flow)
    calc_cp_7dadm_m1 <- cp_temp_delta(bf$cp_7dadm_m1, q, bf$obs_flow)
    
    feat <- data.frame(
      cp_flow_mean = q,      
      cp_7dadm     = calc_cp_7dadm,
      Julian       = bf$Julian, 
      air_max      = bf$air_max,
      air_min      = bf$air_min, 
      cloud_pct    = bf$cloud_pct,
      cp_flow_m1   = q,      
      cp_7dadm_m1  = calc_cp_7dadm_m1,
      air_max_m1   = bf$air_max_m1, 
      air_min_m1   = bf$air_min_m1,
      dadm_m1      = bf$dadm_m1
    )
    
    tibble(
      lead_days     = bf$k, 
      run_date      = bf$run_date,
      obs_cp_7dadm  = bf$cp_7dadm,      # observed (actual current conditions)
      calc_cp_7dadm = calc_cp_7dadm,    # adjusted for hypothetical flow q
      obs_flow      = bf$obs_flow, 
      flow_cfs      = q,
      pred_7dadm    = as.numeric(predict(rf, newdata = feat))
    )
  })
})

# "for each forecast horizon, what is the minimum flow needed to meet the temperature target, and how far are we from that flow today?"
threshold_df <- sweep_df |>
  group_by(lead_days) |>
  mutate(crosses = any(pred_7dadm <= target_C)) |> 
  filter(if_else(crosses, pred_7dadm <= target_C, pred_7dadm == min(pred_7dadm))) |>
  slice_min(flow_cfs, n = 1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(flow_gap = round(flow_cfs - obs_flow))

# what does the model predict at current flow?
obs_pred_df <- sweep_df |>
  group_by(lead_days) |>
  slice_min(abs(flow_cfs - obs_flow), n = 1) |>
  ungroup()
```

```{r anchor-sweep-plot, fig.cap="**Figure 5.** Predicted RM 8.5 7DADM as a function of sustained Camp Polk flow at each forecast lead, with all non-flow conditions fixed at their observed values for the anchor event. Dashed red line = 20°C HCP threshold. Vertical dotted lines = minimum sustained flow needed to reach the threshold (shown only where achievable). Filled circles = model prediction at the flow that actually occurred on each run date."}
lead_colors <- c("1" = "#D4A853", "3" = "#C07038", "7" = "#185FA5")
lead_labels <- c("1" = "1-day lead", "3" = "3-day lead", "7" = "7-day lead")
threshold_crossings <- filter(threshold_df, crosses)

ggplot(sweep_df, aes(x = flow_cfs, y = pred_7dadm,
                     color = factor(lead_days), group = factor(lead_days))) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = target_C, linetype = "dashed",
             color = "#c0392b", linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = flow_range[[1]] + 2, y = target_C + 0.15,
           label = paste0(target_C, "°C HCP threshold"),
           hjust = 0, color = "#c0392b", size = 3.2) +
  { if (nrow(threshold_crossings) > 0) list(
      geom_vline(data = threshold_crossings,
                 aes(xintercept = flow_cfs, color = factor(lead_days)),
                 linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 0.8, show.legend = FALSE),
      geom_label(data = threshold_crossings,
                 aes(x = flow_cfs, y = target_C - 0.45,
                     label = sprintf("%.0f cfs", flow_cfs),
                     color = factor(lead_days)),
                 size = 3, show.legend = FALSE, label.padding = unit(0.15, "lines"))
  )} +
  geom_point(data = obs_pred_df,
             aes(x = flow_cfs, y = pred_7dadm, color = factor(lead_days)),
             size = 3.5, shape = 16) +
  { if (nrow(threshold_crossings) == 0)
      annotate("text", x = mean(flow_range), y = target_C - 0.5,
               label = "Threshold not achievable within observed flow range\n(atmospheric driver dominates)",
               hjust = 0.5, color = "grey40", size = 3.2, fontface = "italic")
  } +
  scale_color_manual(values = lead_colors, labels = lead_labels, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(title    = sprintf("RF flow sweep — %s exceedance event", format(anchor_date, "%b %d, %Y")),
       subtitle = "Air temp & cloud fixed at observed values | Camp Polk water temp co-varied with flow",
       x = "Camp Polk sustained flow (cfs)", y = "Predicted 7DADM at RM 8.5 (°C)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r anchor-action-table, echo=FALSE}
threshold_df |>
  transmute(
    `Days before exceedance` = lead_days,
    `Action start date`      = format(run_date, "%b %d, %Y"),
    `Observed flow (cfs)`    = round(obs_flow),
    `Flow needed (cfs)`      = round(flow_cfs),
    `Increase required (cfs)` = flow_gap,
    `Threshold reachable`    = if_else(crosses, "Yes", "No — atm. driver")
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    caption = sprintf(
      "Table 2. Minimum Camp Polk flow to hold RM 8.5 7DADM at or below %.1f°C, by how far in advance the flow action begins. 'Action start date' is the day the increase would need to begin.",
      target_C
    )
  )
```

```{r anchor-key-finding, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
any_cross <- any(threshold_df$crosses)
if (any_cross) {
  best  <- threshold_df |> filter(crosses) |> slice_min(flow_cfs, n = 1)
  worst <- threshold_df |> filter(crosses) |> slice_max(flow_cfs, n = 1)
  cat(sprintf(
    "**Key finding:** Acting **%d days** before the exceedance, a sustained Camp Polk flow of **%.0f cfs** (+%.0f cfs from observed) is estimated to hold RM 8.5 7DADM at or below %.1f°C.",
    best$lead_days, best$flow_cfs, best$flow_gap, target_C
  ))
  if (nrow(filter(threshold_df, crosses)) > 1) {
    cat(sprintf(
      " Waiting until **%d day(s)** prior increases the required flow to **%.0f cfs** (+%.0f cfs) — the same event becomes harder to manage the longer the decision is delayed.\n\n",
      worst$lead_days, worst$flow_cfs, worst$flow_gap
    ))
  } else { cat("\n\n") }
} else {
  cat(sprintf(
    "**Key finding:** No Camp Polk flow within the observed range (%.0f–%.0f cfs) can bring RM 8.5 7DADM below %.1f°C for this event at any lead time. Atmospheric conditions (air temperature, solar load) are the dominant driver — flow management alone cannot achieve compliance for an event of this magnitude.\n\n",
    flow_range[1], flow_range[2], target_C
  ))
}
```

## 4. Does This Pattern Hold Across Years?

The worked example above describes one event. This section runs the same RF flow sweep — with Camp Polk water temperature
co-varied with flow — across all **`r nrow(rm85_dadm_all |> filter(dadm_7 > target_C, !is.na(dadm_7)))`
historical exceedance days** (2012–2025) to ask: for how many events is flow management
effective, and does effectiveness depend on when in the summer the exceedance occurs?

```{r seasonal-sweep-setup}
exceed <- rm85_dadm_all |>
  filter(dadm_7 >= target_C, !is.na(dadm_7)) |>
  mutate(year = year(date), julian = yday(date))

flow_mean_lkp <- camp_polk_flow_historical |>
  filter(statistic == "mean") |> select(date, flow_cfs)

cp_temp_lkp <- camp_polk_temperature_historical |>
  filter(statistic == "7DADM") |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) |> select(date, cp_7dadm = temperature)

# TODO = flagging this as a potential issue since it's not grouping 
# by lead days 
wx_daily <- all_historical_forecasts |>
  group_by(valid_date, variable) |>
  summarise(value = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = value)

flow_range_hist <- quantile(camp_polk_flow_historical$flow_cfs, c(0.05, 0.95), na.rm = TRUE)
flow_grid_hist  <- seq(flow_range_hist[1], flow_range_hist[2], length.out = 100)

models_hist <- map(lead_days_vec, function(k) {
  readRDS(file.path(model_dir, sprintf("rm85_rf_7dadm_lead%d.rds", k)))
}) |> set_names(lead_days_vec)
```

```{r seasonal-sweep-run, cache=TRUE}
all_feats <- expand_grid(exceedance_date = exceed$date, lead_days = lead_days_vec) |>
  mutate(run_date = exceedance_date - lead_days,
         julian   = yday(exceedance_date),
         year     = year(exceedance_date)) |>
  left_join(flow_mean_lkp |> rename(run_date = date, cp_flow_mean = flow_cfs), by = "run_date") |>
  left_join(flow_mean_lkp |> mutate(run_date = date + 1) |>
              rename(cp_flow_m1 = flow_cfs) |> select(-date), by = "run_date") |>
  left_join(cp_temp_lkp |> rename(run_date = date), by = "run_date") |>
  left_join(cp_temp_lkp |> mutate(run_date = date + 1) |>
              rename(cp_7dadm_m1 = cp_7dadm) |> select(-date), by = "run_date") |>
  left_join(wx_daily |> rename(exceedance_date = valid_date), by = "exceedance_date") |>
  left_join(wx_daily |> mutate(exceedance_date = valid_date + 1) |>
              rename(air_max_m1 = temperature_2m_max, air_min_m1 = temperature_2m_min) |>
              select(exceedance_date, air_max_m1, air_min_m1), by = "exceedance_date") |>
  rename(air_max = temperature_2m_max, air_min = temperature_2m_min,
         cloud_pct = cloud_cover_mean) |>
  left_join(rm85_dadm_all |> mutate(run_date = date + 1) |>
              rename(dadm_m1 = dadm_7) |> select(run_date, dadm_m1), by = "run_date") |>
  filter(complete.cases(pick(cp_flow_mean, cp_7dadm, air_max, dadm_m1)))

# One predict() call per model — vectorized across all events
sweep_results <- map_dfr(lead_days_vec, function(k) {
  rf      <- models_hist[[as.character(k)]]
  feats_k <- all_feats |> filter(lead_days == k)
  n       <- nrow(feats_k)

  flow_rep          <- rep(flow_grid_hist, n)
  obs_flow_rep      <- rep(feats_k$cp_flow_mean,  each = length(flow_grid_hist))
  obs_cp_7dadm_rep  <- rep(feats_k$cp_7dadm,      each = length(flow_grid_hist))
  obs_cp_7dadm_m1_rep <- rep(feats_k$cp_7dadm_m1, each = length(flow_grid_hist))

  big_mat <- feats_k |>
    slice(rep(seq_len(n), each = length(flow_grid_hist))) |>
    mutate(
      cp_flow_mean = flow_rep,
      cp_flow_m1   = flow_rep,
      cp_7dadm     = cp_temp_delta(obs_cp_7dadm_rep,    flow_rep, obs_flow_rep),
      cp_7dadm_m1  = cp_temp_delta(obs_cp_7dadm_m1_rep, flow_rep, obs_flow_rep)
    ) |>
    transmute(cp_flow_mean, cp_7dadm, Julian = julian, air_max, air_min,
              cloud_pct, cp_flow_m1, cp_7dadm_m1, air_max_m1, air_min_m1, dadm_m1)

  all_preds <- as.numeric(predict(rf, newdata = big_mat))
  pred_mat  <- matrix(all_preds, nrow = n, ncol = length(flow_grid_hist), byrow = TRUE)

  feats_k |>
    mutate(
      min_pred_7dadm = apply(pred_mat, 1, min, na.rm = TRUE),
      threshold_flow = map_dbl(seq_len(n), function(i) {
        idx <- which(pred_mat[i, ] <= 20)
        if (length(idx) > 0) flow_grid_hist[idx[1]] else NA_real_
      }),
      fixable = !is.na(threshold_flow)
    ) |>
    select(exceedance_date, lead_days, julian, year,
           obs_flow = cp_flow_mean, min_pred_7dadm, threshold_flow, fixable)
})
```

```{r seasonal-fixability-table, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
sweep_results |>
  group_by(lead_days) |>
  summarise(n_events = n(), n_fixable = sum(fixable),
            pct_fixable = round(100 * mean(fixable), 1),
            med_threshold = round(median(threshold_flow, na.rm = TRUE)),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  transmute(`Lead (days)` = lead_days,
            `Exceedance events` = n_events,
            `Flow-fixable` = n_fixable,
            `% fixable` = paste0(pct_fixable, "%"),
            `Median threshold flow (cfs)` = med_threshold) |>
  knitr::kable(
    caption = "Table 3. Proportion of all historical 7DADM exceedance events where a Camp Polk flow within the observed range is sufficient to hold RM 8.5 7DADM ≤ 20°C, by forecast lead. 'Median threshold flow' is the median minimum flow needed among fixable events."
  )
```

```{r seasonal-rate-plot, fig.cap="**Figure 6.** Smoothed probability that a flow action can prevent an RM 8.5 7DADM exceedance"}
sweep_results |>
  mutate(lead_f = factor(paste0(lead_days, "-day lead"),
                         levels = c("1-day lead", "3-day lead", "7-day lead"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = julian, y = as.integer(fixable), color = lead_f)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", span = 0.4, se = TRUE, alpha = 0.15) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("1-day lead" = "#D4A853", "3-day lead" = "#C07038", "7-day lead" = "#185FA5"),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(152, 166, 182, 196, 213, 227, 244),
    labels = c("Jun 1", "Jun 15", "Jul 1", "Jul 15", "Aug 1", "Aug 15", "Sep 1"),
    limits = c(155, 255)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(-0.05, 1.05)) +
  labs(title    = "Probability that a Camp Polk flow action prevents exceedance",
       subtitle = "Smoothed over all historical exceedance days, 2012–2025",
       x = "Day of year", y = "Proportion of events that are flow-fixable") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")
```

Two patterns emerge from the historical record:

- **Early-season exceedances** are more often flow-fixable.
  Air temperatures are moderate enough that additional cool water from Camp Polk can
  offset thermal loading at RM 8.5.
- **Peak-summer exceedances** are increasingly
  atmosphere-dominated. During the hottest periods, no Camp Polk flow within the
  historical range can prevent exceedance — the thermal signal is driven by air
  temperature and solar radiation, not hydrology.

---

## 5. The Actionable Lead-Time Window

Flow-fixability is necessary but not sufficient — the decision also has to happen early
enough. This section asks: **for each historical exceedance, how far in advance does a
flow action need to start to still be effective?**

```{r lead-window-analysis}
lead_windows <- sweep_results |>
  group_by(exceedance_date, julian, year) |>
  summarise(
    max_fixable_lead = if (any(fixable)) max(lead_days[fixable]) else 0L,
    any_fixable      = any(fixable),
    min_threshold    = min(threshold_flow, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups          = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    window_label = case_when(
      max_fixable_lead == 7 ~ "Fixable: action needed ≥7 days prior",
      max_fixable_lead == 3 ~ "Fixable: action needed ≥3 days prior",
      max_fixable_lead == 1 ~ "Fixable: action needed 1 day prior",
      TRUE                  ~ "Atmosphere-dominated: no flow achieves compliance"
    ),
    window_label = factor(window_label, levels = c(
      "Fixable: action needed ≥7 days prior",
      "Fixable: action needed ≥3 days prior",
      "Fixable: action needed 1 day prior",
      "Atmosphere-dominated: no flow achieves compliance"
    ))
  )
```

```{r lead-window-table, echo=FALSE}
lead_windows |>
  count(window_label) |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) |>
  transmute(`Actionable window` = gsub("\n", " ", as.character(window_label)),
            `Exceedance events` = n,
            `%` = paste0(pct, "%")) |>
  knitr::kable(
    caption = "Table 4. Distribution of historical exceedance events by the latest forecast lead at which a Camp Polk flow action is predicted to achieve compliance."
  )
```

```{r lead-window-plot, fig.height=5, fig.cap="**Figure 7.** Each historical exceedance day plotted by calendar date and year. Color shows the latest forecast lead at which a flow action is still predicted to achieve compliance. Atmosphere-dominated events (red) cluster in the peak summer period; events manageable with a 7-day lead (blue) are more common earlier in the season."}
window_colors <- c(
  "Fixable: action needed ≥7 days prior"              = "#185FA5",
  "Fixable: action needed ≥3 days prior"              = "#C07038",
  "Fixable: action needed 1 day prior"                = "#D4A853",
  "Atmosphere-dominated: no flow achieves compliance" = "#C93312"
)

ggplot(lead_windows, aes(x = julian, y = factor(year), color = window_label)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = window_colors, name = "Latest actionable lead",
                     guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3))) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(152, 166, 182, 196, 213, 227, 244),
    labels = c("Jun 1", "Jun 15", "Jul 1", "Jul 15", "Aug 1", "Aug 15", "Sep 1")
  ) +
  labs(title    = "Actionable lead-time window for Camp Polk flow management",
       subtitle = "Each point = one historical 7DADM exceedance day | 2012–2025",
       x = "Day of year", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "right",
        legend.text = element_text(size = 8))
```

---

## Summary

Three operational takeaways:

1. **Flow actions are most useful before mid-July.** After roughly Julian day 200 (July 19),
   atmospheric conditions frequently dominate regardless of Camp Polk releases. Expecting
   flow management to hold compliance during the hottest weeks is often unrealistic.

2. **Earlier is cheaper.** For events where flow management can work, acting 7 days in
   advance typically requires less flow than waiting until 3 days prior — because the
   7-day average has more time to be influenced. The required increase grows the longer
   the decision is delayed.

3. **The window closes fast.** Across historical exceedances, a meaningful fraction are
   fixable at the 7-day lead but not the 1-day lead. A forecast that shows an impending
   exceedance should trigger an immediate decision, not a wait-and-see approach.
